question_text: A bus (80 km/h) overtakes a truck (60 km/h). Truck has 20 km head start. When does bus catch up?

hint_ladder.title: Relative Speed
hint_ladder.text: Parehong direksyon kaya bawas: 80 km/h - 60 km/h = 20 km/h. Ito ang bilis ng paglapit ng bus sa truck.

hint_ladder.title: Catch-Up Formula
hint_ladder.text: Gamitin: Oras = head start / relative speed. Dito, 20 km / 20 km/h = 1 oras.

hint_ladder.title: Compute Time
hint_ladder.text: 20 ÷ 20 = 1. Kaya sagot ay 1 oras. Tignan kung may option na 1h, yun ang B.

hint_ladder.title: Avoid Miscalculations
hint_ladder.text: Huwag pagsamahin ang bilis (80+60) dahil magkaiba 'yon. Bawas dapat. At huwag gamitin ang 60 lang na bilis ng truck.

A.text: You might have chosen A because you added the speeds (80+60=140) then divided 20/140≈0.14h, rounding to 0.5.

B.text: Correct. Relative speed 20 km/h, time = 20/20 = 1 hour.

C.text: You might have chosen C because you divided 20 km by 60 km/h = 1/3 hr, then mistakenly tripled it, confusing part and whole.

D.text: You might have chosen D because you subtracted speeds as 10 km/h (80-60=10) then 20/10=2h, misapplying operations.

next_time_rule: **Key Takeaway:** Catch-up time = head start distance / (faster speed - slower speed). Always subtract same-direction speeds.
deconstruct_text:
Nasa NLEX ka, pauwi galing Pampanga. May bus na 80 km/h sa likod mo at truck na 60 km/h sa unahan, 20 km ang pagitan. Tuwing oras, lalapit ang bus ng 20 km sa truck (80-60). Kaya’t sa loob ng 1 oras, magkakatabi sila—saktong 1 hour ang sagot.

Madalas magkamali: idinadagdag ang 80+60 kaya 140 km/h, mali ‘yan. O kaya’y ginagamit ang 60 km/h lang (20/60≈0.33 oras) na parang nakatigil ang bus. Hindi ganun; subtract dapat ang bilis dahil pareho silang direksyon.
